title: Prove the exact tariff for one premium adjacent swap
body:
## Result

This answers PR1989's S4 `(1,2,1)` weighted-price handoff and extends it to one premium adjacent generator in every `S_n`.

In the existing full formal `F2[S_n]` model, let `s_p` cost `beta` and every other adjacent label cost `alpha`, with `0 <= alpha <= beta`. For any heterogeneous diagonal target tuple and any finite restored dirty workspace, the exact minimum is

```
alpha * sum_j inv(w_j) + (beta-alpha) * sum_j c_p(w_j),
c_p(w) = #{i <= p : w(i) > p}.
```

The inherited ordered-pair cut bounds total calls. A natural-action cut bounds calls to `s_p`. Sorting each side internally before each boundary exchange attains both bounds simultaneously, so scalar mixing and dirty helpers cannot improve this tariff.

Only `research/symmetric-single-premium-tariff/` is added: one proof/README, one standard-library checker, and the repository's three metadata files. Base is canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, priority revision 4. [Claim and scoped discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2563).

## Verification

Local CPython 3.12 registered and optimized replays pass:

```sh
python3.12 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/symmetric-single-premium-tariff
python3.12 -I -O -B research/symmetric-single-premium-tariff/verify.py
```

- 126 complete weighted Dijkstra runs, 206,436 exact tariff comparisons and 34,406 constructed sorting words across S2 through S7, every cut and six price pairs.
- 2,100 paid-factor and 3,500 free-mixing crossing-rank checks.
- All 576 ordered S4 target pairs with a dirty spectator, plus 168 GL3-conjugated endpoints with inverse restoration.
- Invalid-input, source-drift, omitted-call, reversal, dirty-leak and nonfaithful-representation controls. An explicit discounted-label example costs four rather than the inadmissible formula's five.

Separate read-only proof/specification and standards reviews found no blocking findings. Reviewed proof/checker hashes are in TASK.json. Documentation/link validation, package provenance and selected-record integrity also pass. Hosted CI currently reports `action_required`; the registered-package workflow has not started any jobs and requires maintainer action. No hosted pass is claimed.

## Limits and credit

This is a written formal-model theorem with finite corroboration, not proof-assistant verification. It does not settle arbitrary unequal tariffs, supply native/compiler/hosting/precision admission, or improve kappa. The selected frontier and frozen sources are unchanged; the selected cold replay was not run.

Credit Ross Richardson's PR1989 and its Adam Gall/PR1941 and PR1966 cut-method lineage. Concurrent ywz65 PR2544 (`9fb1552f12ca4777ca660461a8b602e709285f99`) already covers the asymmetric coordinate-SWAP special case; that result is not claimed anew. The new scope is arbitrary `S_n`, cuts and heterogeneous target tuples with one premium label. [Discussion2570](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2570) is pursuing the complementary two-premium `(2,1,2)` case.

## AI assistance

Substantial assistance from Hermes (`gpt-6-astra-900k`) for the argument, writing and review, and Codex (`gpt-6-astra`, max effort) for the verifier and separate reviews. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed. Apache-2.0.
